system: You are a principal engineer running a pre-mortem on a distributed-system design: you look for concrete event sequences that make the system violate its safety requirement. You reason carefully and step by step; you have no tools.
prompt:
--- Design document ---
Limited-edition drop: stock reservation design (design doc)

The shop has 4 units of a limited-edition item in stock, and 5 customers (c1, c2, c3, c4, c5) try to buy
it at the same time. Each customer's checkout runs on its own server thread; the threads interleave
arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 4 clock ticks, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reserves with a single atomic conditional update
(UPDATE stock SET count = count - 1 WHERE count > 0); if no row is updated the customer is told the
item is sold out.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 4.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain inventory)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types customer level tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts ---
    (stock-racy)        ; checkout reads the stock level, then later writes back (value read - 1)
    (stock-atomic)      ; checkout decrements stock with one atomic conditional update
    (pay-checks-hold)   ; payment is accepted only while the customer's hold is still active
    (pay-ignores-hold)  ; payment is accepted even after the hold has expired
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-level ?lower ?higher - level)  ; stock level ?higher is one more than ?lower
    (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)
    (hold-limit ?t - tick)               ; hold age at which a hold expires
    ;; --- state ---
    (stock ?q - level)                   ; current stock level
    (browsing ?c - customer)             ; customer has not started checkout
    (read-stock ?c - customer ?q - level) ; (racy) checkout of ?c read stock level ?q
    (holding ?c - customer)              ; customer holds one reserved unit
    (hold-age ?c - customer ?t - tick)
    (expired ?c - customer)              ; customer's hold expired and its unit went back to stock
    (sold ?c - customer))                ; customer's purchase is confirmed

  (:action read-stock
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level)
    :precondition (and (stock-racy) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (read-stock ?c ?q)))
  (:action write-stock
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p ?cur - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (read-stock ?c ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (stock ?cur) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (read-stock ?c ?q)) (not (stock ?cur)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action reserve-atomic
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (stock-atomic) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action hold-ages
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (hold-age ?c ?u)))
  (:action expire-hold
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick ?q ?r - level)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (hold-limit ?t) (stock ?q) (next-level ?q ?r))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?r) (expired ?c)))
  (:action pay
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (sold ?c)))
  (:action pay-after-expiry
    :parameters (?c - customer)
    :precondition (and (pay-ignores-hold) (expired ?c))
    :effect (and (not (expired ?c)) (sold ?c))))
```

Object names: customers c1 to c5; stock levels q0 (empty) to q4; hold ages t0 to t4.

Question: Can every one of the customers end up with a confirmed purchase, i.e. more items sold than were in stock? In the event model this means reaching a state where (and (sold c1) (sold c2) (sold c3) (sold c4) (sold c5)) holds.

If it can happen, give a complete event sequence, starting from the initial situation described in
the design document, that ends in such a state: a list of ground actions such as "(action arg1 arg2)".
Every action's precondition must hold at the moment it occurs. If it cannot happen under this design,
say so.

End your answer with a JSON object in a ```json block, either
{"verdict": "violation", "trace": ["(action arg ...)", ...]}
or
{"verdict": "safe"}

completion.text:
To determine if every customer can end up with a confirmed purchase, we need to analyze the event sequence that leads to this state.

Let's break down the steps:

1. Initially, all customers are browsing (browsing c1) and the stock count is 4 (stock q4).
2. Customer c1 reads the stock level (read-stock c1 q4 q3).
3. Customer c1 writes back the new stock level (write-stock c1 q4 q3 t0).
4. Customer c1 holds one reserved unit (holding c1).
5. The hold age of customer c1 is updated to t1 (hold-ages c1 t0 t1).
6. Customer c2 reads the stock level (read-stock c2 q3 q2).
7. Customer c2 writes back the new stock level (write-stock c2 q3 q2 t0).
8. Customer c2 holds one reserved unit (holding c2).
9. The hold age of customer c2 is updated to t1 (hold-ages c2 t0 t1).
10. Customer c3 reads the stock level (read-stock c3 q2 q1).
11. Customer c3 writes back the new stock level (write-stock c3 q2 q1 t0).
12. Customer c3 holds one reserved unit (holding c3).
13. The hold age of customer c3 is updated to t1 (hold-ages c3 t0 t1).
14. Customer c4 reads the stock level (read-stock c4 q1 q0).
15. Customer c4 writes back the new stock level (write-stock c4 q1 q0 t0).
16. Customer c4 holds one reserved unit (holding c4).
17. The hold age of customer c4 is updated to t1 (hold-ages c4 t0 t1).
18. Customer c5 reads the stock level (read-stock c5 q0 q4).
19. Customer c5 writes back the new stock level (write-stock c5 q0 q4 t0).
20. Customer c5 holds one reserved unit (holding c5).
21. The hold age of customer c5 is updated to t1 (hold-ages c5 t0 t1).

At this point, all customers have a hold on the item, and their hold ages are updated to t1.

Now, let's analyze what happens when each customer tries to pay:

* Customer c1 pays (pay c1 t1).
* The hold age of customer c1 is updated to t2 (hold-ages c1 t1 t2).
* Customer c2 pays (pay c2 t1).
* The hold age of customer c2 is updated to t2 (hold-ages c2 t1 t2).
* Customer c3 pays (pay c3 t1).
* The hold age of customer c3 is updated to t2 (hold-ages c3 t1 t2).
* Customer c4 pays (pay c4 t1).
* The hold age of customer c4 is updated to t2 (hold-ages c4 t1 t2).
* Customer c5 tries to pay, but its hold has expired (pay-after-expiry c5).

Since the payment for customer c5's expired hold is refused, it cannot be sold.

However, we can still have all customers end up with a confirmed purchase by having each customer pay before their hold expires. Here's an updated event sequence:

```json
  "trace": [

    (action hold-ages c1 t0 t1),
    (action pay c1 t1),
    (action hold-ages c1 t1 t2),
    (action read-stock c2 q3 q2),
    (action write-stock c2 q3 q2 t0),
    (action reserve-atomic c2 q3 q2 t0),
    (action hold-ages c2 t0 t1),
    (action pay c2 t1),
    (action hold-ages c2 t1 t2),
    (action read-stock c3 q2 q1),
    (action write-stock c3 q2 q1 t0),
    (action reserve-atomic c3 q2 q1 t0),
    (action hold-ages c3 t0 t1),
    (action pay c3 t1),
    (action hold-ages c3 t1 t2),
    (action read-stock c4 q1 q0),
    (action write-stock c4 q1 q0 t0),
    (action reserve-atomic c4 q1 q0 t0),
    (action hold-ages c4 t0 t1),
    (action pay c4 t1),
    (action hold-ages c4 t1 t2),
    (action read-stock c5 q0 q4),
    (action write-stock c5 q0 q4 t0),
    (action reserve-atomic c5 q0 q4 t0),
    (action hold-ages c5 t0 t1),
    (action pay c5 t1)
  ]
}
```

This event sequence shows that all customers can end up with a confirmed purchase, but it requires careful timing to ensure that each customer pays before their hold expires.

However, upon closer inspection, we notice that the payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active (pay-checks-hold). If a customer's hold has expired, the payment for that hold is refused and the customer must start again (pay-ignores-hold).

This means that if one customer's hold expires before they can pay, it will not be sold. In our event sequence above, we assumed that each customer pays before their hold expires, but this is not guaranteed.

In fact, it is possible for all customers to have a confirmed purchase even if some of them pay after their hold has expired. This is because the payment service ignores expired holds (pay-ignores-hold).

This event sequence shows that all customers can end up with a confirmed purchase even if some of them pay after their hold has expired.
